title: The Commander
objective: Keep the camp and Vorne's daughter out of a fight. Get the fragment.

default: The Compact has turned the old granary into a headquarters, as briskly as people who have done it in other towns before. There are maps on every wall, a duty roster, and a timetable for messages.

Vorne is at a table when you are shown in. He is bigger than you had pictured from what people said, and less imposing than you had expected from what they said about him. He is a man in his fifties who looks as if he has not slept properly for several weeks and has decided that sleeping is not, at present, the point.
He looks up from his papers as you come in. He makes up his mind about you more quickly than Seriva did, and comes to a different conclusion.
"Sit down," he says. He puts it as a preference, but it is not an invitation. "I am told you went east and came back. I should like to know what you found."

default.text: He begins with the ruins. He knows already.
"My sergeant at the checkpoint thinks you lied to him," he says.

text.commander:
You sit down opposite a fellow officer, or near enough, and the two of you talk as people do who know how to say things plainly without explaining themselves.

"I found the east road," you say. "Harrow. The edge of the forest." You pause. "What exactly are you looking for? If I knew, I could tell you whether I came across it."

His eyes sharpen. He likes having the question turned back on him. "A structure," he says. "Underground, under the forest. Some sort of mechanism. Signs of an older civilisation. Seriva believes it is the source of the affliction."
text.arcane:
Vorne looks at you as a soldier looks at a civilian expert, trying to decide whether you know more than he does, and about what.

"Your field?" he asks.

"Comparative texts," you say. "Old languages. Pre-kingdom artefacts." It is all true, and chosen to sound like a scholar rather than somebody who goes into ruins.

"Seriva said someone of your sort might have gone east," says Vorne. He is letting you know that she foresaw you. You take note of it.
text.ranger:
Vorne looks straight at you. He has no time for polite preliminaries.

"You were in the forest," he says. "I need to know what is in the forest. Not in any mystical sense. What is the ground like? What is in the way? What would my men run into if I sent them east?"

It is a soldier's question. You can answer some of it without giving him anything that matters.
text.cipher:
Vorne is not subtle and does not try to be. He is a blunt instrument, though not a stupid one, and he is pointed in one direction only.

Seriva is the interesting one, not Vorne. But Vorne is the one with thirty soldiers, and that makes him the more pressing.

choices.text: Tell Vorne part of it. Enough to seem helpful, without giving away the ruins.

bonus.label: The Compact does not trust you

success.text:
You tell him about the east road, and Harrow, and the edge of the forest. You describe the ground accurately, in terms a commander could use, and you describe what the curse has done to the land that anyone can see. All of it is true, and none of it tells him about the inner approach or the chamber.

He listens, and asks questions. You answer them honestly where it costs you nothing, and round them where it would.

At the end he says, "You are holding something back." It is not a question.

"Everyone holds something back," you say. "The question is whether what I'm holding back has anything to do with what you need to know."

He considers this, and decides to let it go. For the present.

success_at_cost.text:
You give him enough, and he takes it. But when you have finished, his face tells you he has worked out the distance between what you know and what you have told him. He has put it away to come back to.

"If you find anything else," he says, "I should like to hear about it before you act on it."

failure.text:
He sees the gap in your story quite plainly, and does not trouble to hide that he has seen it.

"You have been in the ruins," he says. "Not just to the edge of them. Inside."

You neither confirm it nor deny it, and he notes that you have not denied it. "I shall find out what is in there," he says, "with your help or without it. The only question is whether it takes me a day or a week."

choices.text: Suggest working together. You have information he needs.

bonus.label: The Compact does not trust you

success.text:
He listens. He is not a man who turns down a proposal out of habit. He weighs it.

"Go on," he says.

You set out the terms. You will tell him what you found in the ruins. He will give you time before the Compact moves on the source, and he will keep Seriva away from the Rootless camp. And he will have what he needs for whatever he is planning.

He looks at you a long while. "You know what is in the ruins," he says.

"Yes," you say.

"And you will tell me."

"The parts that matter to you."

He holds out his hand. You shake it, both of you understanding that this arrangement will not last for ever.

success_at_cost.text: He is willing to talk, but he won't commit himself. You have his attention, and a little time. He will not agree to anything formal until he knows more about what you are offering.

failure.text:
He does not bargain when he doesn't know what he is bargaining for. He needs to know what you have before he will agree to anything.

"When you decide to tell me what you really found," he says, "come back."

choices.text: "Do you know where your daughter is?"

bonus.label: The Compact does not trust you

success.text:
He goes very still.

"What do you know about my daughter?" he says. He has himself perfectly in hand, but underneath it, if you are looking, there is a father who has not been sleeping because his daughter is somewhere he cannot see.

"She's safe," you say. "She's being looked after. She isn't getting any worse." All of it is true.

He looks at you. "Where?" he says. The whole of his authority goes into the one word.

"That depends," you say, "on what you mean to do when you know."

success_at_cost.text:
When you say the word daughter, his face does several things at once.

"She's being looked after," you say. "Somewhere safe from the worst of it." You don't name the camp.

He looks at you a long time. "Tell me where she is," he says.

"When we've talked about what you'll do when you know."

failure.text:
He gives you nothing at all. He has himself perfectly in hand, and he doesn't let anything show. Either he knows already where she is, or he has decided that whatever he feels about not knowing is not for you to see.

"My family is not your concern," he says.

text.default:
The trouble comes in the shape of a Compact soldier at the edge of the Rootless camp.

He is not threatening anybody. He has been sent alone, which is either good manners or a deliberate show of confidence. He has a note from Vorne. It is addressed to Maret, and there is nothing secret in it. Commander Vorne respectfully asks that his daughter be returned to the Compact post, where she will receive proper medical care.

Branch has handed the note over, and Maret is reading it. The camp has been waiting for something like this, and now that it has come, it is not sure whether to be relieved.

Lira is watching from across the camp with the loose attention of the partly afflicted. But her hands have stopped working the rope, so she is paying more attention than she seems to be.
text.commander:
You weigh it up quickly. Vorne has made a formal request rather than a demand, so he has not yet decided to use force. The request is a test of Maret, of where the camp stands, and of whether there is room to settle it by talking before he goes any further.

He has given them half an hour. If there is no answer by then, he will decide what to do next.
text.arcane:
The note is polite in form and a threat in substance. Vorne isn't asking whether Issa will be sent back. He is letting it be known that he knows where she is, and that he regards her being at the camp as something that has to be settled.

What matters is what settling it means to him, and what it means to Maret.
text.ranger:
You watch the soldier as you would watch anyone standing at the edge of a place with a message.

He is ill at ease. He was sent because somebody thought one soldier would look less threatening than ten, but nobody told him what to do if the answer was no. He has no orders for that.
text.cipher:
Vorne isn't being polite. He is being careful. The formal request puts his position on record before things get worse. It shows he tried the reasonable way first, which counts for a good deal when you have to write a report afterwards explaining what you did next.

The camp has about half an hour before the reasonable way turns into something else.

choices.text: Help Maret write an answer that buys time and gives nothing away.

bonus.label: You stayed a day too long in the ruins

success.text:
You and Maret work quickly. The answer says that Issa is being looked after and is no worse; that the care she is getting suits her present condition better than anything the Compact post could give her; and that Maret would like to meet Commander Vorne to talk about how she goes on.

You don't say she won't be coming back, and you don't say she is staying. You only propose a conversation.

Maret sends the answer back with the soldier. Half an hour later a runner comes: Vorne will meet her tomorrow morning, at the Tallow.

You have bought a day.

success_at_cost.text: The answer goes, and Vorne agrees to meet. But the soldier's manner as he leaves suggests there are conditions attached. You have bought a day, though only just.

failure.text: The answer doesn't go down as you hoped. Vorne sends back a note a good deal less polite than the first. He wants his daughter back today, not tomorrow. You have less time than you had.

choices.text: Take Issa to Vorne yourself, so that you have charge of the meeting.

default.text:
You speak to Issa first. She is having a good spell, more herself than yesterday, the words coming more quickly. You explain the position plainly.

"I don't want to go back yet," she says. "The camp's..." She stops. "It's the right place for now. I know it is."

"Your father isn't going to wait for ever," you say.

She looks at you. "I know." She is quiet a moment. "If I go, will you be there?"

"Yes," you say.

You take her to the Compact post. When Vorne sees her, his face is simply a father's, before it is anything else at all.

choices.text: Advise Maret to refuse. Issa stays at the camp.

success.text:
Maret sends a refusal. It isn't hostile; it is exact. Issa is in the camp's care. She chose to come, and she will go when she is ready, and the camp does not hand over the people in its care to soldiers.

The soldier takes the answer and goes. An hour later nothing has happened, and two hours later still nothing. Vorne has heard the refusal and chosen, for now, to leave it there.

You can see why. He cannot use force on a camp with his daughter in it without risking hurting her, and he cannot admit in public that his daughter chose the Rootless over the Compact.

So the standoff holds, for the present.

success_at_cost.text: Maret sends the refusal, and Vorne doesn't move at once. But the soldier who comes back looks like a man who has been given orders he didn't like. The standoff holds for now, though nobody can say for how long.

failure.text:
Vorne moves, though not with force. He issues a formal notice that the Compact holds medical authority in Crestfall and has the means to use it, and that the camp is in breach of the notice about the road. More soldiers appear round the edge of the camp.

Nobody has been hurt. Everybody understands that it may not stay that way.

text.default:
The meeting is at the Tallow. Aldous has been asked to shut for the morning, and he does so without argument, though he doesn't leave. He stands behind his bar polishing things that are already polished.

Vorne sits on one side of a table and Maret on the other. You are there too, and neither of them asks why.

Issa is not there. The meeting is about her, but it is not for her.

Vorne begins. He has himself in hand, but it is costing him a great deal. He has seen his daughter, briefly, in passing, long enough to see what the curse has done to her and what the camp's care has done for her. He is carrying both, like a father who has not been able to do what fathers are meant to do.
text.commander:
You have sat at tables like this before. You watch Vorne at work.

He wants Issa back. He also knows Maret is right, and that the camp is better for her than the Compact post. The two pull against each other, and he is not a man who bears that kind of pull gracefully.

By the end of the meeting, you think, he will have given way on something, and he will not call it giving way.
text.arcane:
The meeting is about Issa, but underneath it is about authority, and who the Rootless camp answers to. Maret is making it clear, by the way she speaks, that the camp answers to nobody in Crestfall as things stand.

Vorne is trying to find a way of putting it that lets him accept this without setting a precedent he could not live with.
text.ranger:
You can read both of them easily. Vorne loves her, under all the command, and hides it less well than he thinks. Maret cares, under all the practicality, and hides it less well than she thinks.

They are having two conversations, the one they are having out loud and the one they need to have.
text.cipher:
This can be won. The trick is to find a way of putting it that lets Vorne feel he has charge of his daughter's welfare, without asking Maret to give up the camp's independence.

The two needn't be at odds. It only wants the right words.

choices.text: Step in, and propose terms that suit them both.

bonus.label: The Compact does not trust you

success.text:
You speak, and they both listen, which is the first surprise.

You propose that Issa stays at the camp, in the camp's care. The Compact will send the camp medical supplies, and so admit formally that it can look after her. Vorne will have word of how she is every day. And in return the camp will be given a Compact notice that recognises it, not one that puts it under the Compact, and protects it from any action in future.

Vorne looks at Maret, and Maret looks at Vorne. Something passes between them that is not quite trust.

"I want to see her," Vorne says. "Today."

"Yes," says Maret. "Come this afternoon."

Nothing is written down. Nothing needs to be. The people who made the agreement will keep it.

success_at_cost.text: They accept the terms in outline, but Vorne adds a condition: a Compact doctor is to see Issa once a week. Maret agrees. It is a small thing to give, and it keeps the peace.

failure.text:
It doesn't work. Vorne won't have the word recognition. If he formally recognised the camp it would make trouble for him in the regional capital. The meeting ends with nothing settled.

They both leave looking as though they have not finished with this conversation.

choices.text: Keep out of it. Let them find their own terms.

default.text:
You keep quiet, and they argue it out for an hour.

What they come to is not elegant. It is what two stubborn people agree to when each of them cares more about what they want for Issa than about winning.

Issa stays at the camp. Vorne may visit. The Compact will not move against the camp while she is there. Neither of them puts anything in writing.

It holds, because neither of them can afford for it not to.

text.default:
Six soldiers arrive at the edge of the camp. Six, not thirty, which may be restraint or may be a test. They state their orders without any hostility: Commander Vorne asks that his daughter be returned at once.

Branch goes to the edge of the camp, and Maret stands beside him. Lira has been taken into the middle of the camp with the others who could not look after themselves.

The soldiers have not drawn their weapons, and neither has Branch. It is still undecided what this is going to turn into.
text.commander:
You go to the front. You don't mean to fight. You mean to manage it.

Six soldiers, sent with a request and not an order. You can see from the way they stand that they hope it will pass off quietly. They were sent because Vorne does not want bloodshed. He wants his daughter. That is a different thing, and it leaves room.
text.arcane:
The curse is stronger in the camp today. There are more people, and more fear, and fear seems to feed it.

You watch Lira from across the camp. It is getting to her. This needs to be settled quickly.
text.ranger:
Six men, and one thing they want. They have been told how to get Issa, and they have been told what not to do to get her.

Somewhere between those two sets of orders there is a way out.
text.cipher:
Six soldiers, and a request. Vorne has left himself a way out. If the camp refuses, the six go home, and the matter goes through the proper channels instead of coming to blows. He is being careful.

The question is what he will do if the proper channels don't give him what he wants.

choices.text: Step forward and talk to the soldiers yourself.

success.text:
You step forward and speak to the man in charge, a sergeant, who is plainly relieved to have somebody to talk to instead of a standoff to keep up.

You arrange that the soldiers will go back to Vorne and ask for a meeting between him and the camp's leaders, a proper one, at the Tallow, tomorrow morning.

He agrees, and the soldiers leave. The standoff is over, and nobody is hurt.

When they have gone Branch looks at you. "That was close," he says.

"It wasn't that close," you say.

"No," he says. "But I am glad you were here."

success_at_cost.text: You get a delay out of them, but not a meeting. The soldiers go back with the message that the camp needs time to talk it over. It is a matter of hours, not days.

failure.text:
It doesn't hold. The soldiers push past the edge of the camp, firmly but not roughly. Branch doesn't stop them, because the only way to stop them would be to fight.

They find Issa in the tent and bring her out. She doesn't resist. As she passes she looks at you, and you will spend a long time afterwards trying to work out what that look meant.

She goes to the Compact post. The camp watches her go.

choices.text: Stand in the gap between the tents, and don't move.

success.text:
You walk into the gap between the two nearest tents and stop there, facing the soldiers. You don't say anything.

The sergeant looks at you, and at Branch beside you, and at the six men behind him, and does the sum. "We'll tell the Commander she's well," he says. "He'll want to talk."

Branch doesn't look at you. He moves half a step nearer.

success_at_cost.text: You stand in the gap. One of the younger soldiers walks right up to you, close enough for you to smell the road on him, and you don't move. The sergeant calls him back. "He'll want to talk," the sergeant says. Your hands don't stop shaking for an hour.

failure.text:
They go round you.

The soldiers push past the edge of the camp, firmly but not roughly. Branch doesn't stop them, because the only way to stop them would be to fight.

They find Issa in the tent and bring her out. She doesn't resist. As she passes she looks at you, and you will spend a long time afterwards trying to work out what that look meant.

She goes to the Compact post. The camp watches her go.

default.text:
"Sergeant. Stand your men down and wait for the Commander's word."

He has his hand up to his men before he has thought about who said it. By the time he does think, it is too late to take it back, and he knows it. "The Commander'll want to talk," he says, to save what he can.

text.default:
Pol finds you when things have settled down enough for the camp to breathe again.

She has the piece of stone. She had it from Issa, with Issa's leave: the piece of the sealing mechanism that Issa found in the outskirts of the ruins, and that Pol has been looking for these three years.

She holds it out. It is about the size of your palm, made of the same dark stuff as the mechanism, half stone and half metal, and it is warm. It is not warm from her hand. It has a faint warmth of its own, like something that remembers working.

"This is what the ritual needs," she says, "besides the two of you. A piece of the mechanism as it was before it was broken. Something that remembers what the mechanism was meant to do."
text.commander:
You look at the fragment and think about what it means. The old ritual cannot be done without it. It is also exactly the kind of thing Seriva will be looking for, and that the Compact will want to get hold of if it ever learns the thing exists, and at present the Rootless camp has it.

The camp has just become a good deal more important than it was this morning.
text.arcane:
You hold the fragment carefully, feeling the warmth of it, and read its residue as closely as you have read everything that mattered since you came to Ashenveld.

The residue is old, and clean. It is older than the curse and older than the break. This piece remembers the mechanism as it was, before Seriva's tampering unsettled it.

You understand now what the ritual does. It uses the fragment to remind the mechanism what it was, and the two people to show it what it might be again.
text.ranger:
The fragment is warm. You take note of it as you would take note of the warmth of the ground in strange country, as a fact rather than a feeling.

"How did Issa find it?" you ask.

"She does not know," Pol says. "She was in the outskirts, looking about, and found it in the soil. The pieces come to the surface sometimes. The mechanism is trying to mend itself. This piece was making its way back to the source."

You think about a piece of broken mechanism making its way home, and about whether it means to, and whether meaning is the right word for what a piece of stone does.
text.cipher:
The fragment changes everything. Now the ritual has all it needs: the two of you, the chamber, and the fragment.

What matters now is timing. Seriva is looking for the chamber. Vorne's soldiers are on the east road. And [missing person] is waiting in the ruins.

"How long before Seriva finds the chamber?" you ask Pol.

Pol thinks. "She knows roughly where it is from twenty years ago," she says. "The outskirts have changed. She will find it, but it will take her time. Days. Perhaps a week." She pauses. "We have less than that."

choices.text: Take the fragment back to the ruins, and tell [missing person] the ritual can go ahead.

default.text:
You take the fragment from Pol. She lets go of it like somebody putting down a thing she has carried a long way.

"The witness," she says. "Someone must be outside the chamber."

"You," you say.

She nods. "Yes. Me." She looks at the fragment in your hand. "Tell them to be ready. Two days. I need to make ready, and so do you. Two days."

choices.text: Go back to the ruins first, and tell [missing person] what has happened.

default.text:
You leave the fragment with Pol for safe keeping and go east.

You come through the outskirts, past the cairn, to the gate. [missing person] is sitting in their usual place, where they seem to have spent a good part of fourteen months, reading their journal in the grey light.

They look up as you come. They read your face and put the journal down.

"Tell me," they say.
